items.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020
items.q: You’d look out there and there’s Judy Garland. She’d come and sit in with the band.

ctx.x: Yeah, when you entered the studio scene, was it mostly by recommendation that you get into that?

The way it happened was quite unusual in that when Buddy Rich’s band played and we recorded the “West Side Story” thing at the Shea and in L.A., we were there for four weeks and when we had every night, every show was sold out. Every show for four weeks. I mean it was never empty. And it was movie stars. You’d look out there and there’s Judy Garland. She’d come and sit in with the band. Johnny Carson would sit in

and play a tune with the band. Milton Berle is right there you know. All of the movie stars. Edie Adams bought the whole club out one night for her personal friends. And you’d look and it was just like you were in the movies, you see all of these movie stars in the place you know. But what happened was Terry Gibbs came in several times, ‘cause of course he loved Buddy and all of that. And Terry liked the way I played lead trumpet. And he always remembered it. And Al Porcino was his lead player in those days, and…
